api:
<NodeGraph> draws a directed graph: services and the calls between them, pipeline stages, dependencies. Nodes are circles with two stats inside, a title below and coloured arc sections around them; edges are arrows that can carry stats of their own. It is a port of Grafana's Node graph panel; see Coming from Grafana.

Edges whose source or target id is not among the nodes are left out.

Arcs and colours

Each node's outline is drawn from its arcs values, in the order of the chart's arcs sections, clockwise from the top:

  • A value of 1 or more paints the whole outline in that section's colour.
  • Otherwise each non-zero value takes that share of the circle. Shares past 100% are cut off.
  • A node without non-zero arcs gets its color, or grey.

The legend lists the sections. Clicking a section switches to the grid layout sorted by it; click again to reverse the order.

Layouts

NodeLayoutPlacement
Layered (default)left to right in layers, so every edge points right where it can; crossings are reduced; loops are allowed
Forcea physical simulation that pulls connected nodes together and pushes others apart (Grafana's d3-force settings)
Gridrows of nodes in data order, or sorted by an arc from the legend

The buttons in the top-right corner switch layouts at any time.

Node limit. With more nodes than node_limit, the graph shows the nodes nearest the roots (nodes with no incoming edges) and collapses each unexplored branch into a "N nodes" marker. Click a marker to centre the view on that branch. In the grid layout, the limit shows a window of the sorted nodes.

Interaction

  • Pan by dragging the background. Zoom with the + and − buttons, or the mouse wheel: with ZoomMode::Cooperative, hold Ctrl (⌘ on macOS) so the page can still scroll; with Greedy, the wheel always zooms. The ⛶ button resets the view and fits the graph.
  • Hover a node to highlight it and its neighbours, dim the rest, show its full title and the stats of its edges. Hover an edge to show its stats.
  • Click a node or edge for a popover with its title, stats, arc shares and detail rows, or handle the click yourself with on_node_click / on_edge_click.

The graph starts fitted to the panel, never zoomed in past 100%.

Differences:

  • Grafana lays out every node and then applies the limit; here only the shown nodes are laid out, so a limited graph stays compact.
  • The graph starts fitted to the panel instead of at 100%.
  • Node icons and fixed node positions are not available.

examples.title: Service map
examples.description: Services left to right in layers, with success and error arcs. Hover a node or an edge.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn service_map() {
    let nodes = use_signal(services(1));
    let edges = use_signal(calls(1));
    rsx! { <NodeGraph nodes={nodes} edges={edges} arcs={health()} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Node colours
examples.description: No arcs: each node's outline in its own colour.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn colors() {
    let palette = [
        0x1e66f5, 0x40a02b, 0xdf8e1d, 0x8839ef, 0xd20f39, 0x04a5e5, 0xea76cb, 0x179299,
    ];
    let nodes = use_signal(
        services(4)
            .into_iter()
            .zip(palette)
            .map(|(node, color)| node.arcs([]).color(rgb(color)))
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    let edges = use_signal(calls(4));
    rsx! { <NodeGraph nodes={nodes} edges={edges} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Highlighted
examples.description: A highlighted node and the edges into it.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn highlighted() {
    let nodes = use_signal(
        services(5)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|node| {
                let hot = node.id().as_ref() == "payments";
                node.highlighted(hot)
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    let edges = use_signal(
        calls(5)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|edge| {
                let hot = edge.target().as_ref() == "payments";
                edge.highlighted(hot)
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <NodeGraph nodes={nodes} edges={edges} arcs={health()} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Edge styles
examples.code:
#[component]
fn edge_styles() {
    let nodes = use_signal(services(6));
    let edges = use_signal(
        calls(6)
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, edge)| {
                let edge = edge.thickness(1. + (index % 4) as f32);
                if index % 3 == 0 {
                    edge.dashed(true).color(rgb(0x8839ef))
                } else {
                    edge
                }
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <NodeGraph nodes={nodes} edges={edges} arcs={health()} class="h-96" /> }
}

examples.title: Click callbacks
examples.description: on_node_click and on_edge_click instead of the details popover.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn callbacks() {
    let nodes = use_signal(services(8));
    let edges = use_signal(calls(8));
    let picked = use_signal(SharedString::Borrowed("Click a node or an edge."));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-96">
            <div class="text-xs">{picked.get()}</div>
            <NodeGraph
                nodes={nodes}
                edges={edges}
                arcs={health()}
                on_node_click={move |node: &GraphNode, _: &mut Window, _: &mut App| {
                    picked.set(SharedString::from(format!("Node {}", node.id())));
                }}
                on_edge_click={move |edge: &GraphEdge, _: &mut Window, _: &mut App| {
                    picked.set(SharedString::from(format!("Edge {} → {}", edge.source(), edge.target())));
                }}
                class="flex-1"
            />
        </div>
    }
}

examples.title: Number formats
examples.code:
#[component]
fn numbers() {
    fn rate(value: f64) -> SharedString {
        format!("{value:.0} req/s").into()
    }
    fn latency(value: f64) -> SharedString {
        format!("{value:.1} ms").into()
    }
    let nodes = use_signal(
        services(9)
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, node)| {
                node.main_stat(50. + noise(index as u64) * 500.)
                    .secondary_stat(noise(index as u64 + 30) * 80.)
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    let edges = use_signal(
        calls(9)
            .into_iter()
            .enumerate()
            .map(|(index, edge)| {
                edge.main_stat(noise(index as u64 + 60) * 20.)
                    .secondary_stat(SharedString::default())
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! {
        <NodeGraph
            nodes={nodes}
            edges={edges}
            arcs={health()}
            formats={StatFormats::new().node_main(rate).node_secondary(latency).edge_main(latency)}
            class="h-96"
        />
    }
}

examples.title: Live data
examples.description: Signals as data: the stats update in place.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn live() {
    let round = use_signal(1u64);
    let nodes = use_signal(services(1));
    let edges = use_signal(calls(1));
    rsx! {
        <div class="flex flex-col gap-2 h-96">
            <div
                id="refresh"
                class="cursor-pointer text-sm underline"
                onClick={move || {
                    let next = round.get() + 1;
                    round.set(next);
                    nodes.set(services(next));
                    edges.set(calls(next));
                }}
            >
                "Refresh the stats"
            </div>
            <NodeGraph nodes={nodes} edges={edges} arcs={health()} class="flex-1" />
        </div>
    }
}
